body:
**Not ready for an agent.** The shape of this work is still a design question, and one dependency has to land before any of it can start.

## The gap

A finished import job writes its accepted rows, its rejected rows and a manifest, but nothing in the app renders any of that for a person. A rejected row records the reason and the offending cell and nothing else: no severity, no error class, no suggested fix. An operator who wants to know whether a job needs attention has to open the raw files and work it out.

## Blocking dependency

The redaction pass that strips personal data from import artifacts is not yet applied to rejected rows. A report built before that lands would be a second, larger copy of the same leak.

## Candidate ticket shapes

1. A structured rejection record with a severity and an error class, rendered from fields only, never from free-text narrative.
2. A `widgets report <job>` command that prints a job summary from those fields.
3. An eligibility filter so intentionally blank columns are not reported as errors.

## Next step

Turn this into a spec, then into tickets. Do not generate tickets from this body directly.
